name: Sylvan-Sabkha
description: Rock deserts and sand seas take turns under a sky like hammered brass. Between dust events the wind redraws a nearby asteroid belt, patient as erosion itself.
The air carries wet iron and lichen, and sound behaves strangely: footsteps crack loud, then die without echo. At night the temperature drops fast enough to hear the rock tick as it contracts.
Core samples from the deep crust contain isotopes with no known decay chain. The samples are stored off-world now, and studied reluctantly.
The charts mark this world in cautious amber. Those who ignore the marking tend to come back rich, changed, or not at all.
